transcript: It's always a treat to see big names in small-scale plays, and even better when it doesn't break the bank. Hugh Jackman and Ella Beatty are starring in Sexual Misconduct of the Middle Classes, running downtown at the Minetta Lane Theatre with tickets as low as $35 through lottery and day-of box office sale. This is a story about a married writer-professor and one of his 19-year-old students, told from his point of view in the third person. You can probably guess where this is going, but for a play directly in the realm of the #MeToo era, it's pretty subversive in its form and its complex handling of morality and power dynamics. Hugh Jackman, with his undeniable charisma, narrates the majority of the story directly to the audience, positioning him as a protagonist that the audience would otherwise be rooting for if he wasn't so morally questionable. But although Hugh Jackman has significantly more stage time and lines, than Ella Beatty, she too is giving a really nuanced and unassuming but sharp performance. The arc of her character is really interesting, and Ella portrays her journey so delicately and specifically. This simple but effective production is really easy to appreciate in such a small theater where the actors are not mic’d and are in direct conversation with you. It almost feels like a seminar — a raw and communal experience where inevitably, a myriad of different opinions will surface and float around the room. And when you can cut that type of engaged energy with a knife, you know it's good theatre. With that, another program for my collection.
